newsitem.title: UK: US pressure won't debilitate Cuban economy - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: US pressure won't debilitate Cuban economy - c.bank.

text.p: The U.S. Helms-Burton law has created problems for Cuba but it will not debilitate the country's economy, Cuba's Central Bank president Francisco Soberon told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.
"If the goal (of the Helms Burton law) is to collapse our economy, they are not doing that. It creates problems for us but it is not an obstacle that we cannot overcome," Soberon said.
The Central Bank president said Cuba is growing and has developed new ways to deal with pressures imposed by the United States since the law was enacted.

"Whenever we have a new obstacle, it's a new challenge for us and that makes us work harder. We have to be more efficient, more creative and to think of new alternatives and we are doing that," Soberon said.
The Helms-Burton law was enacted last year to tighten the U.S. embargo against Cuba.
The law seeks to punish foreign firms investing in property seized from U.S. citizens and companies in Cuba after the 1959 revolution that brought President Fidel Castro to power.
Since the law passed, the U.S. government has imposed sanctions on a Canadian mining firm and a Mexican industrial group.

"They feel the only way to deal with Cuba is to punish us and say to others how they should deal with Cuba. They feel they have the right to order others, and of course the world is not prepared to accept that situation," he said.
Soberon said Cuba has already suffered as a result of the Helms Burton law but he added the country is finding new ways to deal with the impact.
He said estimates for the country's economic growth remained at previous targets of four to five percent in 1997, with growth coming from the manufacturing, services and tourism.
